note: What is outstanding on this book, each with where it is argued.

issues.title: Authored prose has no verbatim gate
issues.description: An extraction cannot cite words that are not in the source; authored prose can. Eighteen of twenty-five founder quotations in the workflow document had been smoothed into readability before a script caught them.

issues.title: File paths named in prose are not checked
issues.description: Chapters 4 and 15 named a test file the day it was deleted. The researcher's first debrief named a brief path renamed four releases earlier. Both found by reading.

issues.title: The title is not yet earned by the body
issues.description: The book is called Creating a Book Using Agentic Workflows and its own graph counts workflow six times in 27,002 words. Closing this is what part one and the vocabulary pass are for.

issues.title: Does the cover name Claude?
issues.description: Brief 40 said 'writing a book with Claude'; brief 41 said 'making a book with agents'. The book names Claude four times. The two memos point different ways and it has not been decided.

issues.title: A graph diff needs a graph per book version
issues.description: Only the current version has a graph, so the diff the founder asked for cannot be computed backwards yet. A text diff is available from the tags today and should not be mistaken for the answer.

issues.title: Issues-FS is missing from the network page
issues.description: Logged as task T31 in the v0.3.27 pack and still open. Their site cites this one for the philosophy; this one does not list them at all.

issues.title: The fractal principle's February origin is not credited in prose
issues.description: Part 3 of Thinking in Graphs, written for Issues-FS on 5 February 2026, names and works through the fractal principle five months before the document called Fractal Semantic Graphs. The anchored extraction holds it; the timeline in origins.md does not say it.

issues.title: Per-agent task folders are not built
issues.description: The board shows the workstreams. The day-to-day list each agent owns, on the Issues-FS-lite pattern with the writer rule, does not exist yet.
